messages:
ava_support: Heads-up — Acme reported repeated 429s + high tail latency after a sudden traffic spike this morning. Customer says it looks like "throttling" but requests are small and sequential.

ava_support: Repro steps from them:
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do \n  curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"rwd-3B","prompt":"ping","max_tokens":8}' &
done
```

ava_support: Header they pasted from a sample 429:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: rq_abc123
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 168000
x-retry-after: 2
```

ava_support: They attached a short trace from their side showing lots of tiny responses and some >1s tail latencies. Customer is asking if this is a quota issue or our batching/KV cache behaving poorly.

raj_runtime: @ava_support thanks — can you paste a short snippet of our internal request log (request id) that matches one of their 429s? I want to correlate with batching traces and kv cache metrics.

ava_support: Pasted internal log (from alert ingestion):
{"ts":2333339001,"req_id":"rq_abc123","tenant":"acme","model":"rwd-3B","batch_size":1,"kvcache_hit":false,"prefetch":false,"latency_ms":670,"status":429}

maya_sre: Quick hypothesis: continuous batching kept flushing tiny batches (batch_size=1) because KV-cache misses prevented prefix reuse; combined with a burst of parallel sequential requests it hit tenant concurrency/quota controls. That can look like "throttling" but root cause is cold/unshared KV entries + small batches that consume concurrency slots quickly.

maya_sre: Can you also grab batching configuration for their tenant? Particularly flush_timeout_ms, max_batch_tokens, and kv_prefetch config.

ava_support: Tenant config excerpt (from console):
tenant: acme
max_concurrency: 40
continuous_batching:
  enabled: true
  flush_timeout_ms: 30
kv_cache:
  enabled: true
  prefetch_on_miss: false
  prefix_ttl_sec: 0

raj_runtime: Aha — prefetch_on_miss:false + TTL 0. That explains lots of cold misses. Each miss means no cached KV to attach, so KV warmup happens inside the request path, causing slower single-request latency and preventing larger batches from forming (clients retrying or opening parallel connections => concurrency spike). Also each request charged counts toward quota and concurrency; if many come in, we hit rate-limit.

lena_oncall: Immediate mitigation options:
- Enable tenant prefetch_on_miss for a short window (helps warm KV in background)
- Raise prefix_ttl_sec to 60 for this tenant
- Temporarily bump max_concurrency for acct until warmup completes

lena_oncall: I'll open a short task to apply prefetch flag + ttl 60 for acme and increase concurrency to 80 for 10 minutes. @raj_runtime / @maya_sre any objections?

raj_runtime: fine with TTL + prefetch. Also recommend increasing flush_timeout_ms to 80ms for this tenant to allow batching to coalesce few requests into larger batches (reduces per-token overhead). That should lower tail latency and reduce 429s.

maya_sre: +1. Also we should add a quick check in alerting: detect sustained stream of batch_size==1 and kv_cache_hit==false patterns per-tenant and surface as "cold-kv warmup" so support can triage faster.

ava_support: I told the customer the eng team will try config changes and monitor. They want repro steps for their devs to avoid this: suggested smooth ramp (<= concurrency 20), enable client-side retry backoff, and send a warmup sequence (one priming request with a longer prompt) before bursts.

ava_support: Customer asked if changing model variant helps — they run rwd-3B. Any note?

raj_runtime: Smaller model variants can reduce per-token time but won't fix cold-kv misses. If they use a variant with smaller KV footprint or quantized variant that has faster kernel startup, that helps marginally. Primary fix is prefetch/ttl and batching timeout tuning.

lena_oncall: Action items:
- Apply tenant changes (prefetch=true, prefix_ttl_sec=60, max_concurrency=80) — in progress
- Adjust flush_timeout_ms to 80ms for acme — planned
- Add alert rule for "kv-cold-warmup" pattern — follow-up

deploy-bot: Started runbook: apply-tenant-config:acme — job id jb_98765 — ETA 45s

deploy-bot: Completed job jb_98765 — prefetch=true, prefix_ttl_sec=60, max_concurrency=80 applied

maya_sre: Observing metrics — within 3 minutes we see kv_cache_hit rate for acme rising from ~12% -> ~74% and batch_size P50 from 1 -> 12. Tail latency dropping. 429 rate down to ~0.3% from 8%.

ava_support: Customer confirmed improvement in their test harness after config change. They still want guidance doc for warmup patterns; I'll draft a short note and share.

raj_runtime: I'll open a short runtime PR to default prefetch_on_miss=true for tenants that have continuous_batching enabled (with safety guard). Also add telemetry to detect this pattern automatically.

ava_support: Thanks all — closing the escalation with customer. cc: @maya_sre for follow-up alert rule, @raj_runtime for PR.

maya_sre: noted. filing follow-up ticket INF-4421 for alert + docs.

ava_support: :thumbsup:
